reason: Grouping fibres seems like a useful first step toward building the opposing muscles.
expectation: I expect a bundle or group of muscle fibres, though it may still need connective tissue.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the triceps also advances the goal, but I want to build up the other muscle first.

effect: The fibres formed the expected bundle, which can now be combined with connective tissue.
reaction: The connection from one fibre to a bundle is clear, though unsurprising.
reason: Adding the sheaths seems like the next step in organizing the fibres into a muscle.
expectation: I expect a wrapped muscle bundle or a more complete muscle.

alternatives.reason: The triceps could be attached now, but I want to finish building the fibre bundle first.

effect: The sheaths produced a biceps with tendons, showing how connective tissue carries the fibres’ pull to bone.
reaction: The explanation that muscle pulls rather than pushes makes the need for opposing muscles clearer.
reason: Attaching the biceps continues the muscle I just built and advances the arm goal.
expectation: I expect the biceps tendons to attach to the arm skeleton so the muscle can help bend the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but I want to connect the newly built biceps first.

effect: The biceps is attached and shown bending the elbow; the assembly still needs an extensor.
reaction: The paired poses make the biceps’ pull clear.
reason: The triceps fits the remaining extensor slot and is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach opposite the biceps and help straighten the elbow.

effect: The triceps completes the opposing muscle pair and shows how the elbow can straighten.
reaction: The opposing pulls make sense after the explanation that muscles cannot push.
reason: Adding blood vessels is the only offered combination and should supply the arm.
expectation: I expect a vascularized arm assembly, with blood vessels supplying its tissues.

effect: The vessels complete the arm and connect its muscles to the earlier discussion of cellular energy; their ends still await a larger circulation.
reaction: The link between blood supply and working muscle cells is useful, although the result gives little explanation of what the vessels deliver.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and learning that muscles pull rather than push made the need for an opposing triceps clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Grouping fibres into a bundle was clear but predictable, and the result added little beyond the action itself.

surprise.text: The connective tissue sheaths produced a complete biceps with tendons; I had expected a wrapped bundle or a more complete muscle, but not necessarily the named biceps.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the menu supplied the compatible combinations, so I did not have to work out which parts fit.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in continuing to see how circulation connects to the arm and its energy needs. The opposing-muscle explanation was clear, though several steps felt predictable.
